lessons.title: Boss: The Ice-Cup Challenge
lessons.goal: 整合實驗步驟、數據與討論，判斷證據能支持到什麼程度
lessons.story:
THE ICE-CUP CHALLENGE

[Experiment plan]
Four students wanted to learn which covering slowed ice from melting. They placed equal masses of ice in four identical cups. Each cup was wrapped with one layer of a different material: paper, cotton cloth, aluminum foil, or nothing. All cups stood on the same classroom table. After thirty minutes, the students measured the melted water.

[Results]
Paper: 32 mL
Cotton cloth: 18 mL
Aluminum foil: 24 mL
No covering: 40 mL

[Team discussion]
Mina: Cotton cloth produced the least water, so it kept the ice coldest.
Leo: Yes, under these test conditions. We should not claim that cloth is always best.
Kai: Why not?
Leo: We tested only one layer in one classroom. Sunlight, material thickness, or a longer test might change the result.
Mina: Then our report should include the exact numbers and the limits of our test.
Kai: Next time, let's compare the materials in sunlight and shade, but keep the cup type and amount of ice the same.

words.example: The students used four identical cups.
Each cup had a different covering material.
They measured the melted water after thirty minutes.
Do not claim more than the results show.
The report should include the exact numbers.

questions.prompt: What did the students change among the four cups?
questions.explanation: 四個杯子的冰量、杯型、位置與時間相同，刻意改變的是外層材料。
questions.evidence: Each cup was wrapped with one layer of a different material: paper, cotton cloth, aluminum foil, or nothing.

questions.prompt: When did the students measure the melted water?
questions.explanation: 實驗計畫明確指出三十分鐘後測量融化的水量。
questions.evidence: After thirty minutes, the students measured the melted water.

questions.prompt: Which cup had the least melted water?
questions.explanation: 結果表中棉布杯為 18 mL，是四組中最低的數值。

questions.prompt: How much more water melted in the uncovered cup than in the cotton-cloth-covered cup?
questions.explanation: 無覆蓋為 40 mL，棉布為 18 mL，兩者相差 40−18＝22 mL。
questions.evidence:
Cotton cloth: 18 mL
Aluminum foil: 24 mL
No covering: 40 mL

questions.prompt: Why were all four cups placed on the same table?
options: To make differences in location less likely to affect the results.
To make every covering the same material.
To melt all the ice before measuring it.
To prove that classroom tables stay cold.
questions.explanation: 把杯子放在相同位置可減少光線、氣流或溫度位置差異，使材料比較較公平。
questions.evidence: All cups stood on the same classroom table.

questions.prompt: Why does Leo avoid saying that cotton cloth is always best?
options: The cloth cup contained more ice than the others.
The group forgot to record any numbers.
questions.explanation: 這次只測一層材料與一個教室環境，證據不足以推廣到所有情況。
questions.evidence: We tested only one layer in one classroom.

questions.prompt: Detective: What does “identical” most likely mean in the experiment plan?
questions.explanation: 為了公平比較覆蓋材料，四個杯子本身必須完全相同，因此 identical 是「完全相同的」。
questions.evidence: They placed equal masses of ice in four identical cups.

questions.prompt: Which conclusion is best supported by this experiment?
options: Cotton cloth prevents ice from ever melting.
Aluminum foil is the best covering in every place.
Under the tested classroom conditions, cotton cloth produced the least melted water after thirty minutes.
Any cup without a covering will produce exactly 40 mL of water.
questions.explanation: 正確結論需包含本次條件、時間與量測結果，不能把單次實驗誇大成永遠或所有地點都成立。
questions.evidence:
Mina: Cotton cloth produced the least water, so it kept the ice coldest.
Leo: Yes, under these test conditions.

questions.prompt: Which new plan would best test whether sunlight changes the results?
options: Use different cup sizes and different amounts of ice in one place.
Repeat the test with equal sets in sunlight and shade while keeping other conditions the same.
Place only the cloth-covered cup in sunlight and measure it next week.
Ask students which material looks coolest without melting any ice.
questions.explanation: 要檢查日照影響，應只改變日照／陰影條件，其餘杯型、冰量、材料與時間維持一致並進行對照。
questions.evidence: Next time, let's compare the materials in sunlight and shade, but keep the cup type and amount of ice the same.
